stem: Meera shines a torch so that several parallel light rays fall on three different mirrors in her science lab at school: a plane mirror, a concave mirror and a convex mirror. Which row correctly describes how the parallel rays are reflected by all three mirrors?

options.text: All three mirrors reflect the parallel rays as parallel rays, because each ray obeys the law of reflection.
The plane mirror keeps the rays parallel, the concave mirror makes them converge, and the convex mirror makes them diverge.
The plane mirror keeps the rays parallel, the concave mirror makes them diverge, and the convex mirror makes them converge.
The plane mirror makes the rays converge, the concave mirror keeps them parallel, and the convex mirror makes them diverge.

teacher.key_rationale: A plane mirror reflects parallel rays as parallel rays; a concave (converging) mirror brings parallel rays together at its focus; a convex (diverging) mirror spreads parallel rays apart. Only option B matches all three behaviours. Option A is the trap for a student who reasons only from the law of reflection for individual rays and drops the condition that surface shape determines the overall beam pattern.
